title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' continuing La Longue Marche. Notation:
- \hat\Pi_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} over Q-bar, a free profinite group of rank 2.
- M_{0,3}^! is an extension of a group N by \hat\Pi_{0,3} acting through inner automorphisms. N contains Γ_Q (Galois action).
- M_{0,3}^{!~} is the bigger group that also accounts for the S_3 symmetry of {0,1,∞}. Its generators are ρ (order 3, cyclic permutation of the cusps) and σ_∞ (the involution fixing ∞). \hat\varphi is a further distinguished automorphism; the page and the next one suggest it is an involutive/S_3-type symmetry.

What the page does.
1. It restricts to M^{!≈}, the elements u that commute (fully, 'intimement'/'entièrement') with \hat\varphi. This is the inverse image of N^{!≈}, giving the extension (24): 1 → \hat\Pi → M^{!≈} → N^{!≈} → 1, with Γ_Q ⊂ N^{!≈}.
2. The previous page produced a canonical section: the stabiliser/normaliser of the 'inertia at 0' data, tied to the choice of a uniformiser z (or −z) at 0. In modern terms this is a tangential base point at 0. Its image is the subgroup M^{!≈}(0) ≅ N^{!≈} (25).
3. Concretely, M^{!≈}(0) = {u_g : g ∈ \hat\Pi solving (14),(15)}. Here u_g is the automorphism determined by its effect on the generators: per the next page, u_g(ρ) = gρ and u_g(σ_∞) = g l_1^{-ν} σ_∞.
4. Every element of M^{!≈} is then written uniquely as int(f^{-1}) ∘ u_g with f ∈ \hat\Pi. This gives the semidirect product (26)-(27): M^{!≈} = M^{!≈}(0) ⋉ Inn(\hat\Pi). Uniqueness uses that the free profinite group has trivial centre.
5. This element is identified with the u_{g,f} = u_{α,β,f} of (19). The parameters α, β are recovered from g by 'trivialising' g as a coboundary for each finite cyclic symmetry (29):
   - α ρ(α)^{-1} = g, for the order-3 symmetry ρ;
   - β σ_∞(β)^{-1} = g l_1^{-ν}, for the order-2 symmetry σ_∞, with ν ∈ Z^ a 'cyclotomic-type' exponent.

What it serves. Grothendieck is parametrising the group of 'S_3-symmetric' automorphisms of \hat\Pi_{0,3} that contain Γ_Q. Modulo inner automorphisms and a choice of tangential base point, these are given by pairs (exponent, element g) satisfying a 3-cycle cocycle relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 and a 2-cycle relation. This is structurally the Drinfeld–Ihara description of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, GT^ ⊂ Out(\hat F_2) lifted to Aut via tangential base points, as pairs (λ,f) with the 2- and 3-cycle relations. The 'micro-probabilisation' on the next page re-expresses the group as the set of ξ (or α) satisfying (30).
errors: The existence of α with αρ(α)^{-1} = g (and of β for σ_∞) is a nonabelian H^1 triviality statement for Z/3 (resp. Z/2) acting on a profinite group. It is not automatic in \hat\Pi itself. Grothendieck takes α in the enlarged group \hat\Pi^~ (next page), where the cocycle condition ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 is what makes this work. α is only determined up to ρ-fixed elements, and the page does not discuss this non-uniqueness.
The page asserts u_{g,f} 'will be exactly' u_{α,β,f} of (19) without verification. The compatibility of the two trivialisations, with the twist by l_1^{-ν}, is left implicit.

The previous page leaves open which uniformiser (z or −z) defines the canonical section. The 'canonical' subgroup M^{!≈}(0) therefore depends on an unresolved sign choice, flagged by Grothendieck himself ('Il faudrait y revenir!').

ideas.what: Canonical splitting of the extension of the 'arithmetic' symmetry group by \hat\Pi_{0,3}, obtained by fixing a uniformiser (tangent vector) at the cusp 0.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base point; splitting of the outer Galois action into an action on \hat F_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'), Ihara, Anderson
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme speaks of base points 'à l'infini' informally; this precise form is unsure

ideas.what: Semidirect product decomposition M^{!≈} = M^{!≈}(0) ⋉ Inn(\hat\Pi_{0,3}), with unique writing int(f^{-1}) ∘ u_g.
ideas.modern_name: Aut-lift of GT^: GT ⋉ Inn(\hat F_2) inside Aut(\hat F_2)

ideas.what: Parametrisation of symmetric automorphisms by g satisfying a 3-cycle relation (ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1) and a 2-cycle relation involving σ_∞ and an exponent ν.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (2-cycle and 3-cycle relations on (λ,f))
ideas.where_published: Only the program is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the equations themselves are not published

ideas.what: Writing the cocycle-type solution g as a coboundary, g = αρ(α)^{-1} and g l_1^{-ν} = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}, in an enlarged group.
ideas.modern_name: Trivialisation of the 2-/3-cycle relations: f = g(y,x)^{-1} g(x,y)-type 'square root' presentations of GT elements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 (remark on f in the 2-cycle relation); later Lochak–Schneps, Furusho

missed.claim: Grothendieck, independently of and probably before Drinfeld/Ihara, sets up the GT-type parametrisation of S_3-compatible automorphisms of \hat\Pi_{0,3}. It consists of a section given by a tangential base point at 0, a semidirect decomposition with inner automorphisms, and two cyclic-symmetry relations.
missed.quote: on peut donc écrire M_{0,3}^{!≈} comme un produit ½ direct M_{0,3}^{!≈} ≃ M_{0,3}^{!≈}(0)·\hat\Pi_{0,3}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context for GT^. The archive confirms Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets' is a version of the GT relations, worked out in detail. Experts (e.g. Schneps) suspect this, but it is not documented in print.

missed.claim: The S_3 relations are expressed as coboundary conditions in an enlarged orbifold group \hat\Pi^~ (α with αρ(α)^{-1} = g, β with βσ_∞(β)^{-1} = g l_1^{-ν}). This frames GT membership as simultaneous triviality of nonabelian Z/3 and Z/2 cocycles.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a cohomological reformulation of the 2-/3-cycle relations via the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient M_{0,3}/S_3. This could be compared with known 'square-root' presentations of GT elements and with Hilbert-90-type arguments; the explicit coupling of both symmetries is not standard.

missed.claim: The sign/normalisation of the canonical uniformiser at 0 (z vs −z), and hence of the canonical section, is left undetermined.
missed.quote: Mais est-ce bien le bon? Il faudrait y revenir!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This corresponds to the known choice of tangential base point 01→ versus its negative. It is resolved in the later literature (Deligne, Ihara), so the open question is minor today.

deep.surprise_reason: A detailed, worked unpublished derivation of the GT-type structure (tangential section, semidirect decomposition, 2- and 3-cycle relations with coboundary trivialisations) by Grothendieck, likely predating Drinfeld/Ihara. The mathematics itself is now standard, and his anticipation of GT is suspected by experts.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'commutent ultimement' is doubtful. The image looks more like 'commutent entièrement' or 'intimement' à \hat\varphi.
Under (24) the marks '∪ ‖ Q' most likely denote Γ_Q ⊂ N_{0,3}^{!≈}, consistent with the previous page.
In (27) the parenthesis should read '(u_g ∈ M_{0,3}^{!≈}(0) i.e. u_g = u_g with g sol. de (14)(15))'. 'u_0' is a misreading of the subscript g.
In (29) the second relation is β σ_∞(β)^{-1} = g l_1^{-ν}. The symbol after β is σ_∞, written with the stroke-through, not '≠'.
Page number 420 at top and archive number 238 at bottom left.
